result.summary: The page is largely well-composed, but the bottom navigation state contradicts the visible content: 'Profile' is marked active while a Home/discovery feed is displayed. A couple of smaller inconsistencies exist in the favorite-button treatment and low-contrast placeholder text. Carousel clipping at the right edge and the card cut off at the bottom were treated as intended behavior.

issues.description: The bottom tab bar highlights 'Profile' in green as the active tab, but the screen content is clearly the Home/discovery feed (delivery address, search, category chips, promo banner, restaurant carousels). The active-state indicator does not match the rendered screen.
issues.suggestion: Set the active tab to 'Home' (green icon + label) and render 'Profile' in the inactive gray style, so the navigation state reflects the current route.

issues.description: The favorite (heart) buttons on the 'Popular right now' cards are styled inconsistently: the Tokumaru Ramen Bar card shows a bare white heart outline directly on the photo, while the pizza card below shows the heart inside a translucent dark circular badge. On lighter imagery the bare icon would be hard to see.
issues.suggestion: Apply the same circular scrim/badge background to all favorite buttons so the icon has consistent shape, size and contrast regardless of the underlying photo.

issues.description: The search field placeholder 'Restaurants, dishes, groceries' is very light gray on a light gray fill, giving low contrast that may fail WCAG 1.4.3 for readable text.
issues.suggestion: Darken the placeholder color (e.g. to a mid-gray around #6B7280) or darken the field fill so the text reaches at least 4.5:1 contrast.

issues.description: Card imagery in 'Fastest near you' is visually inconsistent: the first tile uses a bright near-white background while the following tiles use dark blurred backgrounds, making the row look uneven and the first tile's edges blend into the page.
issues.suggestion: Normalize the image treatment (consistent background/blur or a subtle border/overlay on light images) so all tiles in the row read as a uniform set.
